aut

conjunction · Wiktionary

or (one or the other)

The alternatives exclude each other, or the second replaces the first: “this or that, not both” (Lewis & Short). Repeated, aut … aut, either … or. After a negative Latin keeps aut or turns it into nec … nec: “I don’t drink wine or milk” is nec vīnum nec lac bibō.

Other words

  • vel — or (whichever you like)

    conjunction · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 88: maenam āridam vel ōvum dēmittitō; Traupman 354 · Wiktionary

    The choice is free, and either will do: “or, if you like”. Vel potius, or rather.

  • -ve — or (lightly)

    enclitic conjunction, added to the second word · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 14.16: duābus tribusve hōrīs (Lewis & Short); Ter. Ph. 3.3.21: nē quid plūs minusve faxit (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

    A light vel, mostly between numbers and small words: plūs minusve, more or less.

  • sīve (seu) — or, or if

    conjunction · also used · classical · Hor. S. 2.8.16–17: Albānum … sīve Falernum tē magis adpositīs dēlectat, habēmus utrumque · Wiktionary

    “Or if”: in a condition, a second possibility; also a second name for the same thing, “or rather”. For “whether … or” see that record.

  • an — or (in a question)

    conjunction, in direct and indirect questions · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 2.8.1: studēs an piscāris an vēnāris an simul omnia?; Traupman 354 · Wiktionary

    The “or” of a question that offers a choice: Vīnum an aquam?, wine or water?

Examples

  • aniculae saepe inediam bīduum aut trīduum ferunt

    little old women often go without food for two or three daysCic. Tusc. 2.40

  • cavētō, quom ventus siet aut imber, effodiās aut ferās

    take care not to dig up or carry a tree when there is wind or rainCato Agr. 28.1

  • maenam āridam vel ōvum dēmittitō; sī natābit, ea muriēs erit

    drop in a dried sprat or an egg; if it floats, that will be brineCato Agr. 88

  • duābus tribusve hōrīs

    in two or three hoursCic. Phil. 14.16 (Lewis & Short)

  • Albānum … sīve Falernum tē magis adpositīs dēlectat, habēmus utrumque

    if Alban or Falernian pleases you more than what is served, we have bothHor. S. 2.8.16–17

  • studēs an piscāris an vēnāris an simul omnia?

    are you studying, or fishing, or hunting, or all at once?Plin. Ep. 2.8.1

See also either … or, whether … or, otherwise.
